name: Mushroom
summary: Mushroom, a recessive dilution of red pigment caused by a frameshift in MFSD12 on chromosome 7 (c.600dupC, p.Asp201fs). Two copies turn a chestnut into a flat sepia, beige or taupe, often with a flaxen mane and tail, though the flaxen may come with it and not from it. On a bay the red areas may be diluted while the black points stay black, which is less well characterised; a black horse is not expected to show it. One copy shows nothing. Best documented in Shetland Ponies, where the variant matched the colour in all 96 ponies tested, and found at low frequency in Miniature Horses. UC Davis reports the genotypes as N/N, N/Mu and Mu/Mu. No effect on build or performance is established.

phenotypes.name: Mushroom carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy. No visible dilution; the horse passes the copy to about half its foals.

phenotypes.name: Mushroom
phenotypes.description: Two copies. Red pigment is diluted: a chestnut becomes a flat sepia, beige or taupe, often with a lighter or flaxen mane and tail. On a bay the red body may be diluted while the black mane, tail and points stay black, and how reliably that shows is not settled. A black horse has little or no red to dilute and is not expected to show it.
